title: Orchestrator Handoff JSON Schema (orchestrator-handoff-v1)
description: JSON Schema for .orchestrator-handoff.json. Three binding decisions this schema encodes: (1) this artifact is hard-mode-implement-only -- base-mode research/plan/implement return via .return-meta.json plus orchestrate-recover-outcome.sh, never this file; (2) the only writable continuation form is the flat top-level continuation_path string -- the nested continuation_context form is deprecated, read-only-accepted for backward compatibility with pre-change in-flight handoffs, and MUST NOT be written; (3) the canonical blocker shape is the wrap-up/hard-mode shape {phase, target, verbatim_goal, what_was_tried, why_it_failed} -- the schema-doc's older {description, phase, severity} shape is retired because it is read by neither orchestrate engine.

status.description: Outcome of the dispatch. Six-value normative vocabulary shared with return-metadata-file.md and reconcile-task-status.sh's handoff_permits_promotion().

phase.description: Optional, informational. Names which lifecycle phase produced this handoff.

summary.description: One to two sentence human-readable summary. Read unconditionally by both orchestrate engines as dispatch_summary.

artifacts.description: Artifacts produced by the dispatch. Both engines read artifacts[0].path/type/summary unconditionally to decide whether to call skill_link_artifacts. Non-empty is required when status is researched/planned/implemented; an empty array is legal for partial/failed/blocked.

type.description: Artifact kind, e.g. report, plan, summary, handoff.

path.description: Repo-relative or absolute path to the artifact.

summary.description: Optional one-line description of the artifact's content. Documented here for the first time despite every reader site reading artifacts[0].summary.

phases_completed.description: Count of plan phases completed by this dispatch. A zero-on-success value triggers an orchestrator corroboration pass against the plan's phase headings.

phases_total.description: Total plan phases for the task.

blockers.description: Canonical wrap-up/hard-mode blocker shape. description and severity are retired -- verified read by neither engine.

phase.description: Phase number or name the blocker occurred in.

target.description: The file, function, or artifact the blocker concerns. Read by the hard engine's H5 divergence audit and blocked-escalation flow.

verbatim_goal.description: The verbatim goal that could not be achieved. Read by the hard engine's blocked-escalation flow.

what_was_tried.description: What approach(es) were attempted before blocking.

why_it_failed.description: Why the attempted approach(es) did not succeed.

plan_markers_verified.description: Whether the implementer confirmed plan phase-heading markers match the reported phase counts.

skeleton.description: Hard-mode-only field: whether a skeleton (stub/sorry-bearing) structure was produced. Read only by the hard engine.

sorry_inventory.description: Hard-mode-only field: inventory of unresolved sorry/stub markers. Read only by the hard engine.

continuation_path.description: The single canonical, writable continuation pointer -- a path to a handoff or progress artifact the next dispatch should resume from. Null when there is nothing to continue.

continuation_context.description: Deprecated nested continuation form. Accepted on read for backward compatibility with handoffs written before this schema (both engines' dual-form resolution retains this read path deliberately). MUST NOT be written by any writer -- continuation_path is the only canonical write form.

next_action_hint.description: Optional short hint describing the immediate next step for a resuming dispatch.

git_checkpoint.description: Optional git checkpoint reference (commit SHA, snapshot patch path, stash ref, or branch name) recorded at a context-pressure or phase-end handoff.
